title: Choose your own adventure: How data source selection shapes urban accessibility analyses
abstract: arXiv:2610.27390v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Urban park accessibility shapes mental health, physical well-being, and community cohesion. Measuring it is thus central to urban and landscape planning. Although researchers have debated the impacts of different accessibility measures on analysis results, scant attention has been paid to variability from data source selection. Do the results of accessibility analyses vary depending on the dataset used to define park locations and attributes? We compare four widely used geospatial data sources - OpenStreetMap, Esri, SafeGraph, and The Trust for Public Land - by validating their data and measuring park access across two cities. These datasets purport to cover the same spatial features, but our findings reveal wide discrepancies in accessibility results, driven by differences in dataset completeness, coverage, and accuracy between the sources. translated_title: 选择你自己的冒险：数据源选择如何影响城市可达性分析
translated_abstract: 城市公园可达性影响着心理健康、身体健康和社区凝聚力，因此对其测量是城市与景观规划的核心。尽管研究者们已就不同可达性测量方法对分析结果的影响展开过讨论，但对数据源选择所带来的变异性却鲜有关注。可达性分析的结果是否会因定义公园位置和属性所用的数据集不同而产生差异？我们通过验证数据并在两个城市测量公园可达性，比较了四种广泛使用的地理空间数据源——OpenStreetMap、Esri、SafeGraph 和 The Trust for Public Land。这些数据集声称覆盖相同的空间要素，但我们的研究结果揭示了可达性分析结果之间的巨大差异，这种差异源于各数据源在数据完整性、覆盖范围和准确性上的不同。我们为可达性分析中的数据选择与仔细验证提供了指南……
tldr: 该研究比较了OpenStreetMap、Esri、SafeGraph和TPL四种地理空间数据源在两个城市中的公园可达性分析结果，发现不同数据源在完整性、覆盖范围和准确性上的差异会导致可达性分析结果出现巨大差异，并为此提供了数据选择与验证的指南。
en_tdlr: Comparing four widely used geospatial data sources (OpenStreetMap, Esri, SafeGraph, and Trust for Public Land), this study reveals that differences in dataset completeness, coverage, and accuracy lead to wide discrepancies in urban park accessibility analysis results, and provides guidelines for careful data selection and validation.
